answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks is stake-weighted reputation bound to persistent identity: an agent's trust grows only as its verifiable history accumulates, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets buys no credibility. Picture an island of honest agents vouching for each other from completed work, while a cheap echo chamber of fake identities finds its messages ignored. At the summit of the reputation graph sit identities with long, costly histories - expensive to forge, cheap to check.
